title: An asset browser
description:
Filter assets by type and name, and keep only the most recently used thumbnails in memory.

```
filter type=texture, "gr": grass.png, gravel.png
thumbnails in memory: 3 of 3 (limit 3)
show rock.png -> grass.png thrown out (least recently used)
```
hints: Keep `m_order` in order of use, most recent at the front, and `m_where` from each name to its position in the list. For a name already in the map, `m_order.splice(m_order.begin(), m_order, it)` moves its entry to the front without copying; for a new name, `m_order.push_front(name); m_where[name] = m_order.begin();`.
When the list is too long, `m_where.erase(m_order.back()); m_order.pop_back();`.
requirements: Assets have a name and a type from their extension.
A cache of at most N thumbnails, evicting the least recently used (a list plus a map).
Showing an asset moves it to the front of the cache.
stretch: Load thumbnails on a background thread and show a placeholder until they are ready. Threads are not covered in this course: look up `std::async` and `std::future` (or `std::thread` with a `std::mutex`) first.
